evidence.quote: Glue and nail 2 - 1x3" to the back of the planked boards to hold your door together.

R2.reason: Door cleats ("2 - 1x3"") are assembled but have no cut-list row and no length is given. Search: no cutList[].part matches /cleat|brace|batten/ except Shelf braces (13", used for shelves, step 10); the viewed step-4 image shows two long cleats on the door back. Flagged 8"/5"/6" numbers in step 4 are board names; the door boards and 1x2 spacers do have rows (cutList[5], [6], [7]).

R3.reason: Every row is used: sides/bottom support (steps 1-2), top (3), shelves (4, 11), door boards and spacers (5), inserts (7), trim (8), braces/small shelves (11).

R4.reason: Parts 14.5-16" wide come only from the 3/4" sheet (fits 48 x 96); 2.5" and 3.5" parts from 1x3/1x4; door boards 7.25/5.5 and 1.5" spacers can be ripped from the 3/4" sheet. Steps name 1x8/1x6/1x2 stock not listed (see R14).

evidence.quote: Attach both of your sides to the 1x3/bottom support
Cut 1x3" boards and nail to the sides of each cubby.

R5.arithmetic: Sheet: parts wider than any listed board must come from the one 3/4" sheet (48x96 = 4608 sq in): Sides 2x15.5x33 = 1023; Bottom & Middle Shelf 2x15.5x48 = 1488; Top 16x50 = 800; Middle Inserts 2x15.5x23 = 713; Small inside shelves 3x14.5x15 = 652.5. Sum = 4676.5 > 4608 (68.5 sq in over, before the door boards and spacers if those are plywood, and before kerf). 1x3 (steps name 1x3 for these): Bottom support 48 + 6 braces x 13 = 78 -> 126 (+ kerf) > 1 board x 96 = 96, short 30; door cleats ("2 - 1x3"", no length) add more.
R5.reason: Plywood area and 1x3 length both exceed what materials buy (quantity 1 each; Stage 2 recorded no defaulted-quantity flag).

R6.reason: Flagged "3\" nail" is the board name 1x3. Pocket screws 1 1/4" (steps 1-3, 7) match materials[7]; finishing nails (step 8) have no size and materials[10] lists 2" finishing nails; backer nails have no size stated. No two sizes for one use.

evidence.quote: Attach the cabinet doors to the sides using euro hinges. Make sure to leave an even gap around the sides of the doors.

Other positions pass: middle shelf 23 3/8" (step 4), shelf setback "an inch from the front", bottom shelf rests on the bottom support (viewed step-1/2 images), braces "directly in the middle"/personal preference.

R11.reason: No step cites a drawing or "as shown".

evidence.quote: Attach both of your sides to the 1x3/bottom support using 1 1/4" pocket holes screws.
Using the 3/4" setting on your Kreg Jig, make 4-5 pocket holes in the top of your sides as well as 4-5 pocket holes in the bottom and top shelves.
Cut 1x3" boards and nail to the sides of each cubby.

R8.reason: Pocket holes are drilled in step 12 of 13, after steps 1-7 already join the parts with pocket screws; shelf braces (step 11) are nailed inside the cubbies and cabinets after the top, doors and inserts are on and after finishing (step 10). A builder following the order as written cannot drill holes in parts already joined; the build can proceed by reordering, so Fix. Importer preserves page order (import-kreg-plans.mjs steps0.map), so this is Kreg's order.

R9.reason: Step 12 states "the 3/4" setting on your Kreg Jig"; all pocket-hole parts are 3/4" thick.

evidence.quote: The back should be flush. The sides and the front should over hang 3/4".
Lay two 1x8" boards cut to 15.5" long and a 1x6" board cut to 15.5" above them with 1x2"s cut to 15.5" long

R14.arithmetic: (a) Carcass width = shelf 48 (cutList[1]) + 2 sides x 0.75 = 49.5 (shelf sits between the sides in the viewed step-2 image; bottom trim 49.375 corrected agrees). Top = 50 (cutList[2]) -> overhang (50-49.5)/2 = 0.25 per side, not 3/4. Front: top 16 - side depth 15.5 = 0.5, not 3/4. (c) Step 5 uses 1x8, 1x6 and 1x2 boards; search materials for /1x8|1x6|1x2/: none (materials list only 3/4" plywood, 1x3, 1x4, 1/4" backer).
R14.reason: Overhang in step 3 does not match the Top row (needs 51 x 16 1/4 for 3/4" overhangs), and door stock named in step 5 is not in materials (1/4" backer, plywood or 1x2 alternatives are not stated in the steps).
